variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Zig uses `const` for immutable values and `var` for mutable variables, encouraging safety by default.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Zig has explicit arbitrary bit-width integers (e.g., i7, u24) and no hidden control flow.

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: Zig provides standard operators plus special wrapping arithmetic operators like `+%` to handle overflow explicitly.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: `if` statements can be used as expressions, functioning similarly to ternary operators in other languages.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: The `for` loop operates on slices and arrays natively, allowing capture of elements and optional indices.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: Zig's `while` loops can include a continue expression (after the colon) ensuring it runs on every iteration.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Functions use explicit typing. The `pub` keyword makes them visible outside the module.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.notes: Arrays have compile-time known lengths. Slices are commonly used to pass array segments safely.

maps.title: Maps
maps.notes: Maps aren't built into the syntax but are provided by the standard library (`std.AutoHashMap` or `std.StringHashMap`).

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Zig uses error unions (`!T`) instead of exceptions. The `catch` or `try` keywords explicitly handle them.

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.notes: Zig uses C-style // single-line and /* */ multi-line comments.

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Zig provides explicitly sized integer and floating-point primitives with binary and hex support.

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.notes: Zig uses bool / boolean types with true and false literals and logical operators (&&, ||, !).

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Conversion
type_casting.notes: Zig supports explicit type casting using cast operators or constructor functions.

strings.title: Strings & Characters
strings.code:
const str: []const u8 = "Hello, Zig!";
const char: u8 = str[0];
strings.notes: Zig distinguishes between single-character literals and string sequences or pointer slices.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Zig supports string interpolation or printf-style formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching & Switch
pattern_matching.notes: Zig evaluates branching conditions through switch statements, match expressions, or when constructs.

range.title: Ranges & Slicing
range.notes: Zig represents ranges with range operators (.., ..<) or standard indexed iteration boundaries.

iterators.title: Iterators & Sequences
iterators.notes: Zig implements iteration through Iterator interfaces, generators, or range-for loops.

oop_classes.title: Classes & OOP
oop_classes.notes: Zig models object orientation through classes with constructors/encapsulation or structs with associated methods.

lists.title: Dynamic Arrays & Lists
lists.notes: Zig manages growable dynamic collections using vectors, ArrayLists, or dynamically reallocated heap buffers.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Zig represents heterogeneous records through tuples, structured bindings, or lightweight record structs.

sets.title: Sets & Unique Collections
sets.notes: Zig provides unique collection hashing structures with O(1) average lookup and insertion time.

modules_import.title: Modules, Packages & Imports
modules_import.notes: Zig structures namespaces and external libraries via include directives, package declarations, or module imports.
